body.statement: Every E-equivalence class in \(\mathfrak D(V)\) is closed under componentwise binary union of directed and unordered bidirected edges, including both kinds of loops; \(G^\star\equiv_E G\) is its unique greatest member. This strictly extends Manten et al.'s directed theorem to the full finite-DMG class and settles their all-DMG conjecture.
body.justification: It identifies one canonical mixed graph from the E-model.
body.gap: The source proves only the directed theorem and four-node mixed evidence.
body.consumer: Latent cyclic path-space discovery gains a unique maximally informative target.

obligation.what_is_open: Establish unrestricted binary-union closure for two E-equivalent finite directed mixed graphs.
obligation.obstruction: The finite order argument is complete, but it requires unrestricted single-edge transfer.  Antitonicity only controls intervals between comparable equivalent graphs and gives no conclusion for the union of two incomparable representatives.
obligation.attempted: The edges of one representative were enumerated for successive transfer, and the full finite equivalence class was then enumerated for a final union.  This closes every order-theoretic step but leaves the first profile-changing edge addition exactly at the unresolved transfer obligation.  The five-vertex sparse gate found no counterexample but supplies no finite reduction theorem.
obligation.partial_result:
Assuming the still-open unrestricted single-edge transfer theorem, binary-union closure follows without any further graph-theoretic premise.  Given \(G\equiv_EH\), enumerate the finite difference as
\[
 E(H)\setminus E(G)=\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\},
 \qquad K_0=G,\qquad K_r=G+\{e_1,\ldots,e_r\}.
\]
Inductively, \(K_{r-1}\equiv_EH\) and \(e_r\in E(H)\setminus E(K_{r-1})\), so transfer gives \(K_r\equiv_EK_{r-1}\).  Hence \(K_m=G\cup H\equiv_EG\).  Since the full edge universe is finite, the E-equivalence class is finite; iterating binary union over all its members proves that the graph defined in \(\mathrm{def{:}greatest}\) belongs to the class and contains every member.  Antisymmetry gives uniqueness.  Thus the order-theoretic reduction is complete, and its sole missing premise is unrestricted transfer.
